raw_response:
I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou, that is the safest way for me to earn steady grain income and use the land well across the whole year. I already know how to manage wheat and maize, the buyers are easy to find, and the risk is lower than trying a crop with bigger price swings. I do not want to spread myself too thin with many small crops. I will put all my main field into winter wheat first, then follow it with summer maize after harvest.

For the wheat, I will manage it in a practical way, not too fancy and not too light. I will use improved seed, give enough nitrogen for tillering and grain filling, and add phosphorus and potassium so the stand stays even and does not fall over easily. I will irrigate about two times if water is available, mainly around jointing and grain filling, because spring in Hebei can be dry. I will watch closely for aphids, rust, and weeds, and I will spray when needed, but I will not spray excessively because that wastes money.

After the wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize. I will direct-seed or use no-tillage after wheat to save labor, keep moisture, and avoid losing time in the tight planting window. I will still use hybrid maize seed because the yield is more stable for me. I will fertilize enough to support strong growth, then irrigate if summer rain is not enough. I will mainly watch for armyworm, corn borer, and weeds. My goal is not the highest possible yield. My goal is a stable harvest with costs I can control and work I can finish on time.
